item.title: Stability of the TFD Prediction of the Absolute Neutrino-Mass Scale
item.description:
Authors: Karl Heinz Wipfler

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Tensor Field Dynamics (TFD) derives an absolute neutrino-mass scale from its field-intrinsic equilibrium rule and measured neutrino mass-squared differences. The original prediction for the sum of the three neutrino masses is 59.0866 meV. This work examines the numerical stability of this prediction against updated measurement data. The original input values are replaced by data sets from NuFIT 6.0, JUNO, NOvA, and SNO+/PDG while the theoretical computational basis remains unchanged. The resulting mass sums range from 59.0866 to 59.1871 meV, corresponding to a total spread of only 0.1005 meV. The analysis shows that the TFD prediction remains within a narrow range around 59.1 meV despite changes in the experimental input data. This study concerns the numerical stability of the theoretical prediction and does not constitute experimental confirmation of TFD.
